picks.editorial_note: An international team including RWTH Aachen published HydroGym in Nature, a reinforcement-learning platform that lets AI agents actively control fluid flows by embedding physics knowledge directly into the models — a step toward AI-designed control systems for energy, transportation, and defense applications.
picks.title: Training AI Agents that Can Actively Control Fluid Dynamics in Energy, Transportation, and Defense | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: TU Wien physicist Mario Krenn's team showed in Nature that AI can propose novel physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups, demonstrating AI's growing role as a genuine collaborator in fundamental scientific discovery rather than just a data-analysis tool.
picks.title: Artificial Intelligence Suggests New Physics Experiments

picks.editorial_note: NSF is funding a new $30 million Science and Technology Center, led by Michigan State with Georgia Tech among eight partner institutions, to advance predictive AI modeling of turbulence — a foundational problem spanning energy, flight, and basic science.
picks.title: New Center Seeks to Unlock the Science of Turbulence for Energy, Flight, and Discovery

picks.editorial_note: A $7.7 million federally funded partnership between Kansas engineers, the Army Corps of Engineers, and DHS is developing AI-integrated digital twin technology to inspect and strengthen aging American dams — critical infrastructure with direct public safety stakes.
picks.title: Four years later KU researchers continue their work strengthening American dams

picks.editorial_note: HKUST's Generalist-Specialist Collaboration framework pairs a broad medical AI model with lightweight specialist models for precision healthcare, a scientifically strong and highly collaborative approach to clinical AI deployment.
picks.title: Novel AI Framework Unites Generalist and Specialist Models for Precision Healthcare
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: EPFL researchers built a framework that trains AI models to express calibrated uncertainty, or 'doubt,' when proposing experiments — improving automated scientific discovery by teaching AI to know what it doesn't know.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: The Department of Energy awarded a University of Houston-led coalition $2.88 million to use AI for discovering next-generation permanent magnets, directly targeting America's dependence on foreign-controlled critical mineral supply chains.
picks.title: Department of Energy Awards UH-led Team $2.88M to Use AI to Strengthen America’s Critical Mineral Supply Chain | University of Houston

picks.editorial_note: UT Austin's Institute for Fusion Studies is launching interdisciplinary seed grants tied to DOE's new Genesis Mission, which funds applying AI to accelerate fusion energy research — a signal of major federal policy investment in AI-for-energy science.
picks.title: Fusion Energy Seed Grants Launch New Interdisciplinary Collaborations at UT Austin - UT News
picks.university: The University of Texas at Austin

picks.editorial_note: USF, Purdue, and UT Dallas secured a $1.2 million NSF grant to jointly develop quantum-resistant, AI-enabled security for next-generation wireless networks, a notable three-university collaboration on critical infrastructure security.
picks.title: USF faculty secure $1.2M NSF grant to advance quantum-secure, AI-enabled wireless networks

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen received a nationwide German government testing permit for its Level 4 autonomous research vehicle 'karl,' a regulatory milestone that clears the way for real-world validation of AI-driven autonomous driving technology.
picks.title: RWTH Receives Nationwide Testing Permit for Autonomous Research Vehicle “karl.” | RWTH Aachen University | EN
